q: For non-dyadic N (e.g. N=6), our shift-QPE returned grid-approximated eigenphases j/N and would need continued-fractions (CF) post-processing that the paper leaves implicit. What is the minimum counting-register width n(N, epsilon) such that CF recovery of j/N is unique with probability at least 1 - epsilon for the worst-case j?
basis: Experiment 2 with N=6 at n_count=6 produced measured phases at k/64 that are the nearest dyadic rationals to j/6 (max deviation < 2/64). The paper prescribes CF but does not quantify how many counting qubits are needed for unambiguous recovery as a function of N.
next_steps: Implement Shor-style CF post-processing on the shift-QPE outputs, sweep N in {5,6,7,9,10,11,15,21} and n_count in {log2(N)+1, ..., log2(N)+8}, empirically fit unique-recovery probability as a function of (N, n_count), and compare to the classical bound 2 log N + 1.

q: The paper claims certain HSP instances can be solved with a single control qubit (Kitaev iterative phase estimation). Our reproduction verified the coset-input equivalence of QPE and Fourier-view but did not build the 1-qubit iterative variant. For which G, K pairs does the 1-qubit realisation retain polynomial gate complexity when the target eigenvector is only approximately preparable, and how does approximation error propagate through the iterative Kitaev estimation?
basis: Section 5 of the paper (single control qubit / flying qubits). We tested the equivalence numerically for Z_8 but did not implement the 1-qubit variant; the paper is qualitative about how to approximate the required eigenvector target.
next_steps: Implement Kitaev iterative QPE for Z_N shift with approximate eigenvector preparation (e.g. random state fed through amplitude-amplification onto |chi_j>), sweep target-preparation infidelity, measure Bayesian phase-estimate accuracy vs standard QPE for same total gate count.

q: Our HSP-as-QPE identity was exact because 8 is a power of 2 and QFT_{Z_8} is exact. For Z_N with N not a power of 2 the QFT must be approximated (or embedded in a larger power-of-2 Fourier basis). How large is the fidelity penalty, and does the coset-QPE view remain uniformly closer to the ideal HSP distribution than the naive QFT-view under those approximations?
basis: Experiment 3 verified equivalence pointwise to 1e-9 only for N=8. For N=6 we had to embed the shift operator in a dim-8 register (identity on |6>,|7>), which distorts the eigenstructure slightly, and this asymmetry could differentiate the two circuit families.
next_steps: Sweep N in {6,10,12,14,15,21}, implement both (a) approximate QFT with truncation depth log log N and (b) embedded shift-QPE, compare total variation distance to ideal HSP output as a function of QFT truncation.

q: The paper is silent on the sample complexity of recovering K^perp once QPE has been run. In our reproduction we assumed one QPE call sufficed because coset structure was small. How does the classical post-processing (integer Gaussian elimination over K^perp samples) scale when G is a product of many small cyclic factors, and are there noise-tolerant variants that succeed even when 10-20% of QPE samples are corrupted?
basis: We tested only the single-cyclic-factor case G = Z_N. Extending to G = prod Z_{n_i} multiplies the number of samples needed and raises numerical questions the paper does not address.
next_steps: Extend the reproducer to G = Z_2 x Z_2 x Z_4 with hidden K of rank 1 or 2, sweep number of QPE samples, run majority-vote / lattice-reduction post-processing, and empirically map sample complexity vs corruption fraction.

q: Noiseless statevector says QPE-view and QFT-view period-finding are IDENTICAL circuits up to target preparation. Under realistic depolarizing noise, at what per-gate error rate does the practical advantage flip? The two circuits differ in gate count (QPE has n_count controlled-U^{2^k}; QFT-view has one function-oracle call), so real-hardware costs may diverge sharply.
basis: Experiment 3 pointwise equivalence assumed noiseless simulation. The paper motivates equivalence structurally but does not treat noise scaling.
next_steps: Add Qiskit Aer with a depolarizing noise model, sweep per-gate p in [1e-4, 1e-2], run both circuit families for Z_8, d=4, measure TV distance from ideal output distribution vs p, and identify the crossover p at which one variant beats the other.
